Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a is an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations;
c. coercion of unnatural sexual relations, and/or
d. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
(4) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter d includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; and/or
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

Article 10

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 9 letter b shall be carried out in the form of community participation.

(2) Forms of participation as referred to in paragraph (1)

include:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and/or
c. participating in the handling of victims of violence. (3) Forms of participation as referred to in paragraph are carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 3

The objectives of the Protection of Women by the Regional Government include:

a. Preventing all forms of violence against women
b. Providing protection and services to women victims of gender-based violence; and c. Providing services for the recovery of the physical, psychological and economic conditions of women victims of violence.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bungo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Government is the Government of Bungo Regency. 4. Regent hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Bungo.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region,
6. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPAA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of rights. of women victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status group, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the fields of politics, economics, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life. body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic and social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, entrapment of money or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over such other person, whether done within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
12. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman.
14. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious figures, community leaders, customary leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women and gender study centers, mass media or similar others.
15. Private is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.

Violence as referred to in Article 2 paragraph (1) in the form of:

This Regional Regulation comes into effect on the date of promulgation.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 28

(1) The Regional Government through UPTD PPA in conducting Women's Protection utilizes information and reporting systems.

(2) The information and reporting system as referred to in paragraph (1) contains at least:

a. data of Women's Protection partners;
b. reporting of acts of violence against Women;
c. process of implementing Women's Protection; and
d. Women's Protection activities.
(3) Utilization of information and reporting systems as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 11

(1) Protection for Women provided by the Regional

Government includes:

a. prevention;
b. services;
c. empowerment; and
d. coordination of Protection for Women.
(2) Protection for Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government through Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region in the field of women's empowerment.
(3) Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region in the field of women's empowerment in providing Protection for Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall establish UPTD PPA.
(4) Further provisions regarding UPTD PPAA as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VI

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 18

Law as referred to in Article 13 paragraph (2) letter e is to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by:

a. Providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. Accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to fully describe the violence they have experienced; and
c. Coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer assistants, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.
(1) Repatriation

(3) optimizes Women's Protection in the Region. (2) Optimization as referred to in paragraph (1)

includes:

b. maintaining and developing networks and referral systems; and

(3) Optimization of Women's Protection by UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (2) is implemented in accordance with the UPTD PPA code of ethics.
(4) Further provisions regarding the code of ethics as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent's regulation.

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, entrapment of money or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over such other person, whether done within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
12. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman.
14. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious figures, community leaders, customary leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women and gender study centers, mass media or similar others.
15. Private is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.

The objectives of the Protection of Women by the Regional Government include:

a. Preventing all forms of violence against women
b. Providing protection and services to women victims of gender-based violence; and c. Providing services for the recovery of the physical, psychological and economic conditions of women victims of violence.

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

1. Region is Bungo Regency.

8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status group, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the fields of politics, economics, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life. body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic and social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, entrapment of money or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over such other person, whether done within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
12. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman.

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a is an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations;
c. coercion of unnatural sexual relations, and/or
d. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
(4) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter d includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; and/or
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 3

The objectives of the Protection of Women by the Regional Government include:

a. Preventing all forms of violence against women
b. Providing protection and services to women victims of gender-based violence; and c. Providing services for the recovery of the physical, psychological and economic conditions of women victims of violence.

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and/or
c. participating in the handling of victims of violence. (3) Forms of participation as referred to in paragraph are carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a is an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations;
c. coercion of unnatural sexual relations, and/or
d. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
(4) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter d includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; and/or
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

Article 17

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 13. paragraph (2) letter d includes:

a. providing spiritual guidance to victims; and

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 25

(1) The Regional Government supports and facilitates UPTD PPA to conduct cooperation on Women's Protection.

(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1)

is conducted with:

a. the central government;
b. other regency/city governments; and/or
c. the Community.
(3) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted in accordance with legislation. provisions of regulations

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a is an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations;
c. coercion of unnatural sexual relations, and/or
d. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
(4) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter d includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; and/or
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

b. maintaining and developing networks and referral systems; and
c. collecting, compiling and presenting violence reports.
(3) Optimization of Women's Protection by UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (2) is implemented in accordance with the UPTD PPA code of ethics.
(4) Further provisions regarding the code of ethics as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated by Regent's regulation.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BUNGO REGENCY

NUMBER YEAR 2022

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life. body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a is an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations;
c. coercion of unnatural sexual relations, and/or
d. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
(4) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter d includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; and/or
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

Article 11

(1) Protection for Women provided by the Regional

Government includes:

a. prevention;
b. services;
c. empowerment; and
d. coordination of Protection for Women.
(2) Protection for Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government through Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region in the field of women's empowerment.
(3) Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region in the field of women's empowerment in providing Protection for Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall establish UPTD PPA.
(4) Further provisions regarding UPTD PPAA as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 10

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 9 letter b shall be carried out in the form of community participation.

(2) Forms of participation as referred to in paragraph (1)

include:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and/or
c. participating in the handling of victims of violence. (3) Forms of participation as referred to in paragraph are carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 17

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 13. paragraph (2) letter d includes:

a. providing spiritual guidance to victims; and
b. psychological recovery of victims.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitutes services provided by assistants in order to recover the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and to provide social support so that victims have confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems.

Government includes:

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and/or

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bungo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Government is the Government of Bungo Regency. 4. Regent hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Bungo.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region,
6. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPAA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of rights. of women victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status group, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the fields of politics, economics, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life. body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic and social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, entrapment of money or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over such other person, whether done within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
12. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman.
14. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious figures, community leaders, customary leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women and gender study centers, mass media or similar others.
15. Private is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.

Article 26

(1) The Regional Government based on cooperation as referred to in Article 25 forms partnerships in providing Women's Protection.

(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1)

are conducted through:

a. provision of job opportunity information for women victims of violence,
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women victims of violence; and
d. fostering and enhancing economic independence for women victims of violence.

Article 3

The objectives of the Protection of Women by the Regional Government include:

a. Preventing all forms of violence against women
b. Providing protection and services to women victims of gender-based violence; and c. Providing services for the recovery of the physical, psychological and economic conditions of women victims of violence.

Article 34

This Regional Regulation comes into effect on the date of promulgation.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 20

a. Job training;
b. Economically productive enterprises and joint business groups; and
c. Capital assistance.

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a is an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations;
c. coercion of unnatural sexual relations, and/or
d. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
(4) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter d includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; and/or
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status group, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the fields of politics, economics, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life. body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic and social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, entrapment of money or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over such other person, whether done within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
12. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman.
14. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious figures, community leaders, customary leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women and gender study centers, mass media or similar others.
15. Private is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.

Article 3

The objectives of the Protection of Women by the Regional Government include:

a. Preventing all forms of violence against women
b. Providing protection and services to women victims of gender-based violence; and c. Providing services for the recovery of the physical, psychological and economic conditions of women victims of violence.

Article 10

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 9 letter b shall be carried out in the form of community participation.

(2) Forms of participation as referred to in paragraph (1)

include:

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and/or
c. participating in the handling of victims of violence. (3) Forms of participation as referred to in paragraph are carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a is an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations;
c. coercion of unnatural sexual relations, and/or
d. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
(4) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter d includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; and/or
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 11

(1) Protection for Women provided by the Regional

Government includes:

a. prevention;
b. services;
c. empowerment; and
d. coordination of Protection for Women.
(2) Protection for Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government through Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region in the field of women's empowerment.
(3) Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region in the field of women's empowerment in providing Protection for Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall establish UPTD PPA.
(4) Further provisions regarding UPTD PPAA as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bungo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Government is the Government of Bungo Regency. 4. Regent hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Bungo.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region,
6. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPAA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of rights. of women victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status group, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the fields of politics, economics, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life. body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic and social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, entrapment of money or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over such other person, whether done within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
12. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman.
14. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious figures, community leaders, customary leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women and gender study centers, mass media or similar others.
15. Private is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.

(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1)

are conducted through:

c. educational assistance for women victims of violence; and
d. fostering and enhancing economic independence for women victims of violence.

CHAPTER IV

FORMS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN

6.5.text:
Article 7

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a is an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations;
c. coercion of unnatural sexual relations, and/or
d. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
(4) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter d includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; and/or
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bungo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Government is the Government of Bungo Regency. 4. Regent hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Bungo.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region,
6. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPAA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of rights. of women victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status group, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the fields of politics, economics, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life. body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic and social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, entrapment of money or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over such other person, whether done within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
12. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman.
14. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious figures, community leaders, customary leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women and gender study centers, mass media or similar others.
15. Private is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.

Article 34

This Regional Regulation comes into effect on the date of promulgation.

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 11

(1) Protection for Women provided by the Regional

Government includes:

a. prevention;
b. services;
c. empowerment; and
d. coordination of Protection for Women.
(2) Protection for Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government through Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region in the field of women's empowerment.
(3) Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region in the field of women's empowerment in providing Protection for Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall establish UPTD PPA.
(4) Further provisions regarding UPTD PPAA as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

The objectives of the Protection of Women by the Regional Government include:

a. Preventing all forms of violence against women
b. Providing protection and services to women victims of gender-based violence; and c. Providing services for the recovery of the physical, psychological and economic conditions of women victims of violence.

(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a is an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women.

(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c includes:

a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations;
c. coercion of unnatural sexual relations, and/or
d. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
(4) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter d includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; and/or
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the energy or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

Article 26

(1) The Regional Government based on cooperation as referred to in Article 25 forms partnerships in providing Women's Protection.

(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1)

are conducted through:

a. provision of job opportunity information for women victims of violence,
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women victims of violence; and
d. fostering and enhancing economic independence for women victims of violence.

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

Every citizen including women has the same right to obtain a sense of security and freedom from the state to conduct activities in various aspects of life as guaranteed in Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. In reality, there are still many occurrences of gender-based violence against women and violence that treats women disproportionately in various aspects of life, so there is a need for guarantees of women's rights concretely from the government as the state administrator through the regional government supported by various parties. Thus, the Bungo Regency Government as the regional government administrator does not yet have a regional legal product to guarantee women's rights in various aspects of life in Bungo Regency, so it is necessary to establish regulations regarding women's protection as a legal basis so that women's rights in Bungo Regency can be guaranteed in community and state life.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bungo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of Regional Government who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Government is the Government of Bungo Regency. 4. Regent hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Bungo.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the region,
6. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPAA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of rights. of women victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status group, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the fields of politics, economics, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life. body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic and social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, entrapment of money or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person who holds control over such other person, whether done within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
12. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women.
13. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman.
14. Society is individuals, families, communities, religious figures, community leaders, customary leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women and gender study centers, mass media or similar others.
15. Private is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.

Article 11

(1) Protection for Women provided by the Regional

Government includes:

a. prevention;
b. services;
c. empowerment; and
d. coordination of Protection for Women.
(2) Protection for Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government through Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region in the field of women's empowerment.
(3) Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region in the field of women's empowerment in providing Protection for Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall establish UPTD PPA.
(4) Further provisions regarding UPTD PPAA as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

15. Private is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.
